question: What kind of infectious agent causes Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD)?

options.C: A parasitic protozoan in brain tissue
options.D: A mutant strand of DNA virus

explanation: Spot on! CJD is caused by prions, which are unique proteins that misfold and don't even carry DNA or RNA. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h1)

question: What classic structural change happens to the brain tissue in CJD?

options.A: Massive swelling of the blood vessels
options.B: Excessive growth of new nerve endings
options.D: Hardening of the protective skull bone

explanation: Correct! As those rogue proteins build up, they damage the brain cells and leave tiny, sponge-like holes behind. Great job remembering that! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h1)

question: In a healthy human body, where do normal prion proteins naturally live?

options.A: Along the lining of the gut

explanation: You got it! Normal prions hang out peacefully on the surface membranes of our nerve cells. It's only when they change shape that trouble starts. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h2)

question: How do disease-causing prions spread and multiply inside the brain?

options.A: By forcing normal proteins to change shape
options.B: By dividing rapidly through simple cell fission
options.C: By absorbing nutrients from nearby blood vessels
options.D: By replicating their own viral RNA strands

explanation: Spot on! Prions don't reproduce like normal germs; instead, they act like bullies, forcing healthy proteins to fold into the abnormal shape just like them. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which category makes up the vast majority of all CJD cases?
explanation: Correct! Most CJD cases happen sporadically—meaning they appear out of nowhere for no known reason, without any inherited gene or infection link. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h3)

question: How would a patient most likely contract iatrogenic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease?

options.B: Through a mosquito bite in a tropical zone
options.C: By inheriting a mutated genetic trait

explanation: You nailed it! 'Iatrogenic' means it happened accidentally during a medical or surgical procedure, such as using instruments that previously touched infected tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is a very common early physical sign in someone developing CJD?
explanation: Spot on! Sudden, involuntary muscle jerking (called myoclonus) is a classic physical sign as the disease progresses. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h4)

question: In the late stages of CJD, what does the term 'akinetic mutism' mean?

options.A: The patient is completely immobile and unresponsive.
options.B: The patient experiences sudden episodes of paralysis.
options.C: The patient has lost the ability to digest solid food.
options.D: The patient is restless and shouts continuously.

explanation: Correct! Akinetic mutism means the patient can no longer move or speak, remaining entirely quiet and unresponsive to their environment. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which test gives the definitive, 100% confirmation of CJD?
explanation: You got it! While other tests help doctors look at clues, final confirmation requires checking brain tissue for those hallmark sponge-like changes. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why is an MRI scan so helpful when evaluating a patient with suspected CJD?

options.A: It checks the electrical activity of skeletal muscles.
options.B: It reveals characteristic patterns of brain tissue damage.
options.C: It measures the exact level of circulating antibodies.
options.D: It clears away abnormal prion protein deposits safely.

explanation: Spot on! An MRI can show distinct bright spots and damage patterns in specific areas of the brain, guiding the medical team. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary focus of medical care for a patient diagnosed with CJD?

options.C: Restoring lost memory and brain cells

explanation: Correct! Because there is currently no cure for CJD, treatment is all about palliative care—keeping the patient comfortable and easing their symptoms. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h6)

question: As a nurse caring for a bedbound patient in the late stages of CJD, what is your top priority?

options.A: Daily physical therapy to rebuild muscle mass
options.B: Regular position changes to prevent skin breakdown
options.C: Active range of motion exercises for independence
options.D: Frequent neurological testing to track recovery

explanation: You nailed it! Since the patient can't move on their own, turning them regularly is vital to protect their skin from pressure sores. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which of these methods is NOT reliable for destroying infectious prions?
explanation: Spot on! Prions are super tough and survive normal boiling. They need heavy-duty, specialized sterilization protocols to be destroyed. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why do hospitals often prefer single-use instruments for procedures involving suspected CJD patients?

options.A: They are cheaper to purchase in large quantities.
options.B: Standard sterilization fails to eliminate prions reliably.
options.C: Patients prefer disposable tools for surgical safety.
options.D: They prevent the spread of common viral infections.

explanation: Correct! Because standard hospital cleaning methods don't always kill prions, using disposables keeps future patients completely safe. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is the typical life expectancy after CJD symptoms first appear?
explanation: You got it! CJD moves very fast, and sadly, most individuals do not survive past one year after their initial symptoms show up. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h8)

question: How can nurses best support families dealing with a loved one's CJD diagnosis?

options.A: By teaching them how to reverse the disease at home
options.B: By connecting them with palliative care and support
options.C: By promising a full recovery with experimental drugs
options.D: By restricting all visiting hours to prevent stress

explanation: Spot on! A CJD diagnosis is heartbreaking for families. Guiding them to palliative care and emotional support resources makes a world of difference. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h8)
